method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG) 'Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidence-based guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (version 1.4)' (2026 (v1.4; first published 2023)), 23 claims; LICENCE: © RANZCOG, all rights reserved; parts may be reproduced by clinicians, hospitals and medical and allied health organisations without permission, with acknowledgement (read at copyright notice on page 2 of the retrieved PDF). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from World Health Organization (WHO Guidelines Approved by the Guidelines Review Committee), ISBN 9789240104204 'Abortion care guideline, second edition' (2024 (IRIS record issued 31 December 2024)), 8 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO ('Some rights reserved. This work is available under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 IGO licence') (read at copyright page of the WHO IRIS PDF (9789240104204-eng.pdf) and the IRIS dc.rights field). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 adds S2, the WHO Abortion care guideline second edition (2024), fetched as the PDF from WHO IRIS (the NCBI Bookshelf copy, NBK617985, was behind a reCAPTCHA bot check and was not used) and converted with plain pdftotext; claims are anchored to the body text of each recommendation, not the executive-summary table. S1's claims and anchors are unchanged. S2 is CC BY-NC-SA (non-commercial), so it is paraphrased and hash-anchored.

claims.claim: **Give information first:** which tests may be needed, which methods suit the gestation, the benefits and drawbacks of each, what pain and bleeding to expect, the possible complications (including incomplete abortion, ongoing pregnancy and pelvic infection) and contraception afterwards. Explain that abortion is not associated with infertility, cancer or mental-health problems. (Conditional, low certainty)
claims.locator: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG), 'Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidence-based guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (version 1.4)', 2026 (v1.4; first published 2023), https://ranzcog.edu.au/wp-content/uploads/Clinical-Guideline-Abortion-Care.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Women should choose the method they find most acceptable,** free of coercion, once properly informed. Up to 14 weeks, medical and surgical abortion are both safe, effective and acceptable, so a choice can be offered. (Conditional, moderate certainty)
claims.locator: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG), 'Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidence-based guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (version 1.4)', 2026 (v1.4; first published 2023), https://ranzcog.edu.au/wp-content/uploads/Clinical-Guideline-Abortion-Care.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Every part of an early medical abortion service can be delivered by telehealth or face to face.** (Conditional, low certainty) Passing the pregnancy at home can be offered up to 10+0 weeks, depending on preference, clinical need and quick access to urgent care.
claims.locator: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG), 'Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidence-based guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (version 1.4)', 2026 (v1.4; first published 2023), https://ranzcog.edu.au/wp-content/uploads/Clinical-Guideline-Abortion-Care.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Only offer medical abortion where timely medical care can be reached.** Have a clear pathway for retrieval if complications occur (for example aeromedical); in remote areas, inpatient care may suit better.
claims.locator: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG), 'Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidence-based guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (version 1.4)', 2026 (v1.4; first published 2023), https://ranzcog.edu.au/wp-content/uploads/Clinical-Guideline-Abortion-Care.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A clinician with a conscientious objection must say so and tell the woman how to reach the nearest provider** within a clinically reasonable time; the objection must not cause delay, distress or harm.
claims.locator: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG), 'Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidence-based guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (version 1.4)', 2026 (v1.4; first published 2023), https://ranzcog.edu.au/wp-content/uploads/Clinical-Guideline-Abortion-Care.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Haemoglobin and Rh D blood group do not need routine testing** before abortion up to 10 weeks. Use clinical judgement to test selectively where bleeding risk is higher, such as anaemia or a later gestation.
claims.locator: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG), 'Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidence-based guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (version 1.4)', 2026 (v1.4; first published 2023), https://ranzcog.edu.au/wp-content/uploads/Clinical-Guideline-Abortion-Care.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Give anti-D to Rh D negative women whose pregnancy is 10 weeks or more.**
claims.locator: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG), 'Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidence-based guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (version 1.4)', 2026 (v1.4; first published 2023), https://ranzcog.edu.au/wp-content/uploads/Clinical-Guideline-Abortion-Care.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Establish gestational age first,** either clinically (a history that covers the last period, examining or not) or by ultrasound. (Conditional, very low certainty) ⚠️ **Scan when the clinical dating is uncertain, or if symptoms or signs suggest ectopic pregnancy** or another concern; otherwise the decision to scan follows patient preference and service access.
claims.locator: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG), 'Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidence-based guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (version 1.4)', 2026 (v1.4; first published 2023), https://ranzcog.edu.au/wp-content/uploads/Clinical-Guideline-Abortion-Care.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Offer STI screening plus HIV, hepatitis B and syphilis testing to every woman having an abortion,** but do not let it delay care: same-day abortion takes priority. Treat positives and notify partners per local sexual-health guidance.
claims.locator: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG), 'Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidence-based guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (version 1.4)', 2026 (v1.4; first published 2023), https://ranzcog.edu.au/wp-content/uploads/Clinical-Guideline-Abortion-Care.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Mifepristone 200 mg by mouth, then misoprostol 800 mcg buccally, sublingually or vaginally 24–48 hours later.** (Strong recommendation, moderate certainty) Local regulation governs which regimen is used.
claims.locator: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG), 'Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidence-based guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (version 1.4)', 2026 (v1.4; first published 2023), https://ranzcog.edu.au/wp-content/uploads/Clinical-Guideline-Abortion-Care.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **In Australia, early medical abortion is provided up to 9 weeks (63 days)** using the MS-2 Step composite pack (1 × 200 mg mifepristone plus 4 × 200 mcg misoprostol), and **buccal is the only approved misoprostol route here.** New Zealand works to 10 weeks (70 days).
claims.locator: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG), 'Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidence-based guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (version 1.4)', 2026 (v1.4; first published 2023), https://ranzcog.edu.au/wp-content/uploads/Clinical-Guideline-Abortion-Care.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Why this combination:** mifepristone plus misoprostol fails less often than misoprostol alone; 800 mcg is probably the most effective misoprostol dose, and a 24–48 hour gap after mifepristone works best. Buccal or vaginal use leaves fewer ongoing pregnancies than swallowing it.
claims.locator: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG), 'Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidence-based guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (version 1.4)', 2026 (v1.4; first published 2023), https://ranzcog.edu.au/wp-content/uploads/Clinical-Guideline-Abortion-Care.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Offer an antiemetic and analgesia.**
claims.locator: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG), 'Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidence-based guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (version 1.4)', 2026 (v1.4; first published 2023), https://ranzcog.edu.au/wp-content/uploads/Clinical-Guideline-Abortion-Care.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ibuprofen for pain (up to 14 weeks):** one 1600 mg dose (off-label), then 400–600 mg every eight hours, to a ceiling of 2400 mg in 24 hours while pain continues. (Strong, moderate certainty)
claims.locator: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG), 'Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidence-based guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (version 1.4)', 2026 (v1.4; first published 2023), https://ranzcog.edu.au/wp-content/uploads/Clinical-Guideline-Abortion-Care.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Paracetamol can be added:** 1000 mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed, 4000 mg per 24 hours at most, with an antiemetic given 30 minutes before the misoprostol. Opioids only selectively.
claims.locator: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG), 'Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidence-based guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (version 1.4)', 2026 (v1.4; first published 2023), https://ranzcog.edu.au/wp-content/uploads/Clinical-Guideline-Abortion-Care.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No routine antibiotic prophylaxis for medical abortion up to 14 weeks:** serious infection is very unlikely (<1%) and antibiotics carry side effects and resistance risk. (Conditional, very low certainty)
claims.locator: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG), 'Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidence-based guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (version 1.4)', 2026 (v1.4; first published 2023), https://ranzcog.edu.au/wp-content/uploads/Clinical-Guideline-Abortion-Care.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Offer follow-up to rule out an ongoing pregnancy and check for complications;** symptoms alone cannot reliably exclude it. It can be in person, by telehealth, or self-assessed with a urine test.
claims.locator: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG), 'Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidence-based guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (version 1.4)', 2026 (v1.4; first published 2023), https://ranzcog.edu.au/wp-content/uploads/Clinical-Guideline-Abortion-Care.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Urine test:** a negative low-sensitivity urine pregnancy test 14–21 days after mifepristone excludes ongoing pregnancy. **Serum test:** a β-hCG fall of 80% or more, from a level taken within 72 hours of mifepristone to one taken 8–16 days later, excludes it. A positive, invalid or smaller fall needs further investigation.
claims.locator: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG), 'Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidence-based guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (version 1.4)', 2026 (v1.4; first published 2023), https://ranzcog.edu.au/wp-content/uploads/Clinical-Guideline-Abortion-Care.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Incomplete early medical abortion:** options are surgical evacuation, another misoprostol dose, or waiting, chosen by the woman's preference, her symptoms and stability, and access to surgery. (Conditional, very low certainty)
claims.locator: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG), 'Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidence-based guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (version 1.4)', 2026 (v1.4; first published 2023), https://ranzcog.edu.au/wp-content/uploads/Clinical-Guideline-Abortion-Care.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Misoprostol for incomplete abortion:** 800 mcg buccally, repeated as 400 mcg 4 hours later if tissue has not passed. No scan is needed before misoprostol, but one is usually done before surgical evacuation unless bleeding is heavy.
claims.locator: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG), 'Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidence-based guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (version 1.4)', 2026 (v1.4; first published 2023), https://ranzcog.edu.au/wp-content/uploads/Clinical-Guideline-Abortion-Care.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ongoing viable pregnancy:** offer a repeat medical or surgical abortion by preference and access, and warn of the small rise in teratogenic risk from misoprostol if the pregnancy is continued.
claims.locator: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG), 'Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidence-based guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (version 1.4)', 2026 (v1.4; first published 2023), https://ranzcog.edu.au/wp-content/uploads/Clinical-Guideline-Abortion-Care.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Intrauterine contraception:** insert as soon as possible once the pregnancy has passed after medical abortion (or at the time of surgical abortion). **Implant:** insert on the day mifepristone is taken. (Strong, low certainty)
claims.locator: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG), 'Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidence-based guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (version 1.4)', 2026 (v1.4; first published 2023), https://ranzcog.edu.au/wp-content/uploads/Clinical-Guideline-Abortion-Care.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Depot medroxyprogesterone acetate can be given at the time of medical abortion,** even before expulsion, once the small possible added risk of ongoing pregnancy has been discussed.
claims.locator: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG), 'Clinical Guideline for Abortion Care: An evidence-based guideline on abortion care in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand (version 1.4)', 2026 (v1.4; first published 2023), https://ranzcog.edu.au/wp-content/uploads/Clinical-Guideline-Abortion-Care.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **WHO regimen before 12 weeks:** mifepristone 200 mg by mouth, then misoprostol 800 μg vaginally, sublingually or buccally 1–2 days later, at least 24 hours apart. With misoprostol alone, 800 μg by any of those routes. Further misoprostol doses can be used if needed; WHO sets no maximum.
claims.locator: World Health Organization (WHO Guidelines Approved by the Guidelines Review Committee), ISBN 9789240104204, 'Abortion care guideline, second edition', 2024 (IRIS record issued 31 December 2024), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/382157, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **New WHO option: letrozole plus misoprostol** — letrozole 10 mg by mouth daily for 3 days, then misoprostol 800 μg under the tongue on the fourth day (conditional). It may work up to 14 weeks, but it has been compared only with misoprostol alone, not with mifepristone.
claims.locator: World Health Organization (WHO Guidelines Approved by the Guidelines Review Committee), ISBN 9789240104204, 'Abortion care guideline, second edition', 2024 (IRIS record issued 31 December 2024), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/382157, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **WHO (new): no anti-D immunoglobulin for medical or surgical abortion before 12 weeks;** usual anti-D care applies from 12 weeks. Knowing the Rh status is not a prerequisite for early medical abortion. The evidence is very low certainty (two studies, both from 1972).
claims.locator: World Health Organization (WHO Guidelines Approved by the Guidelines Review Committee), ISBN 9789240104204, 'Abortion care guideline, second edition', 2024 (IRIS record issued 31 December 2024), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/382157, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **WHO: ultrasound should not be a prerequisite for abortion** (strong), though it may be used case by case for clinical reasons; WHO notes that gestation limits in law often drive scanning that is not clinically needed.
claims.locator: World Health Organization (WHO Guidelines Approved by the Guidelines Review Committee), ISBN 9789240104204, 'Abortion care guideline, second edition', 2024 (IRIS record issued 31 December 2024), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/382157, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **WHO: a routine follow-up visit is not medically needed after an uncomplicated medical abortion,** provided the woman knows when to return: symptoms of ongoing pregnancy, prolonged heavy bleeding, no bleeding at all, pain that medicines do not relieve, or fever. Low-quality evidence.
claims.locator: World Health Organization (WHO Guidelines Approved by the Guidelines Review Committee), ISBN 9789240104204, 'Abortion care guideline, second edition', 2024 (IRIS record issued 31 December 2024), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/382157, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **WHO recommends offering self-management before 12 weeks,** in whole or in part: judging her own eligibility, taking the medicines without direct supervision, and checking herself that the abortion is complete. The evidence is strongest before 10 weeks, and she must still have accurate information, quality medicines including pain relief, and access to health workers and a facility if wanted.
claims.locator: World Health Organization (WHO Guidelines Approved by the Guidelines Review Committee), ISBN 9789240104204, 'Abortion care guideline, second edition', 2024 (IRIS record issued 31 December 2024), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/382157, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **WHO for incomplete abortion under 14 weeks:** vacuum aspiration or medical management; medically, misoprostol 600 μg by mouth or 400 μg under the tongue. Waiting can work as well as misoprostol if she accepts a longer time to expulsion and a higher chance of incomplete emptying.
claims.locator: World Health Organization (WHO Guidelines Approved by the Guidelines Review Committee), ISBN 9789240104204, 'Abortion care guideline, second edition', 2024 (IRIS record issued 31 December 2024), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/382157, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **WHO on contraception timing:** hormonal methods (pill, patch, ring, implant or injection) can start straight after the first abortion pill; an IUD can go in when the abortion is confirmed complete. Starting DMPA immediately slightly reduces the abortion's success, but it should still be offered.
claims.locator: World Health Organization (WHO Guidelines Approved by the Guidelines Review Committee), ISBN 9789240104204, 'Abortion care guideline, second edition', 2024 (IRIS record issued 31 December 2024), https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/382157, retrieved 2026-09-24
